paper_metadata.title: EAQGA: A Quantum-Enhanced Genetic Algorithm with Novel Entanglement-Aware Crossovers

summary: The paper proposes EAQGA, a gate-based quantum genetic algorithm for portfolio optimization, and evaluates it on a Qiskit MPS simulator for 30- and 40-asset instances and on IBM’s 127-qubit ibm_quebec for a 100-asset instance. EAQGA reports average fitness improvements of 33.6% over classical GA and 37.2% over AQGA on the 100-qubit hardware experiment, and it is also the best of the three methods on the simulator, but the authors explicitly do not claim formal quantum advantage.

experiments.description: EAQGA hybrid quantum genetic algorithm for portfolio optimization evaluated on Qiskit MPS simulator across 10 random subsets of 30 S&P 500 assets and 10 random subsets of 40 assets, with population sizes 10 and 20 over 20 iterations.

algorithm.parameter_initialization: Initial circuits prepared in equal superposition via Hadamard gates; population initialized by measuring the superposition circuits once

problem_formulation.encoding_details: 1 qubit per binary asset-selection variable; circuits generate binary strings by measurement
problem_formulation.objective_function: maximize mu^T x - q * x^T Sigma x subject to x_i in {0,1}
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: binary feasibility inherent in measurement; no additional penalty terms reported

problem_instance.description: Mean-variance portfolio optimization on randomly selected subsets of S&P 500 stocks
problem_instance.dataset_name: S&P 500 / Yahoo Finance via Qiskit Finance

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: historical prices converted to returns Rit = Pit/Pit-1 - 1; mean returns and covariance matrix computed from historical data
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: 10 independent subsets; each algorithm run 100 times per subset; average and standard deviation of fitness reported
